nodes.label: Resumable Staged Audit State Machine
nodes.rationale: Transcribe/acoustic/analyze are separate stages that each persist output so a transient Deepgram/LLM failure resumes mid-pipeline instead of re-running everything. Caveat: default retry count is effectively 1 today per the engineering audit.

nodes.label: Interface + Real + Simulated Device Pattern
nodes.rationale: The standout design decision: every hardware family has a Simulated* implementation swapped in by simulation_mode, so the entire check-in flow runs on a dev machine with no physical hardware and is testable. New work should build on this seam.

nodes.label: Runtime API Keys From Platform Secrets
nodes.rationale: Deepgram/LLM avatar credentials are fetched from the platform's app_secrets at boot (ApiService.GetSecretsAsync) rather than compiled into the binary, so keys can rotate centrally and never ship on a public terminal. One committed-key exception exists per the audit and should be migrated to this pattern.
nodes.norm_label: runtime api keys from platform secrets

nodes.label: Action-less AI Avatar Design
nodes.rationale: The avatar's LLM output is routed only to TTS with no tool/function calling and no path back into processCommand, structurally neutralizing prompt injection as an actuation vector: a guest can at most make it say something off-script, never dispense cash or keys.

nodes.label: Out-of-Process Device Bridge Executables
nodes.rationale: TWRScannerBridge and U10Bridge run as separate executables reached over localhost HTTP to isolate crash-prone native SDKs from the main process; ChildProcessTracker cleans them up on exit.

nodes.label: Embedded Python + Standalone FastAPI Sidecars
nodes.rationale: Vision/ML work is Python-native; embedding CPython via pythonnet keeps OCR/motion in-process while the heavier YOLO11 alert service runs as its own FastAPI process.

nodes.label: frmMainScreen God Form
nodes.rationale: A ~6,900-line single form owning WebView controls, the Socket.IO client, the RELAY dispatcher, Google TTS/Translate, Google Meet, motion streaming, and the AI avatar; documented as a single point of fragility.

nodes.label: Known Engineering Risks (Kiosk)
nodes.rationale: God form fragility, swallow-and-continue global exception handlers with no watchdog, unset WebView2 lockdown flags, dispense commands over an unsigned socket channel, and a committed cloud key in the publish output.

nodes.label: IIDScanner (ID/Passport Reader Abstraction)
nodes.rationale: Multiple implementations (SinosecuLocalScanner, SinosecuSDKScanner, OldScannerBridge, clsIDScanner) exist because deployments use different physical readers with incompatible SDKs; the interface hides that from the command dispatcher.

nodes.label: LicenseStore + HardwareFingerprint
nodes.rationale: DPAPI-encrypted license.dat holds the device secret, bound to a SHA-256 hardware fingerprint of CPU/board/disk serials + MachineGuid so a license cannot be copied between machines.

nodes.label: Hub-and-Spoke Topology (kiotel_web as Hub)
nodes.rationale: kiotel_web is the tower everything talks to: kiosks hold device-authenticated Socket.IO connections for RELAY commands and telemetry; audio services, the PMS partner API, and the ML services all route through the platform rather than talking to each other directly.

nodes.label: Two Databases, Two Hotel/Guest Models
nodes.rationale: There is no shared hotel or guest table across the system: the PMS owns the rich multi-tenant model (customers -> customer_properties -> rooms/guests/reservations) while the platform is device/agent/session centric with a free-text hotelname and per-session guest identity (t_session_info, id_scanjobs).

nodes.label: Check-in-Time Name Match Bridge
nodes.rationale: Because no shared guest table exists, the bridge between PMS and platform identity is matching the OCR'd name from the scan pipeline against t_session_info.guest_name populated per session by an agent or the PMS-autofill extension.
